newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Loyola says no risk of devaluation - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Loyola says no risk of devaluation - paper.

text.p: Brazilian Central Bank President Gustavo Loyola said there was no risk of a strong devaluation of Brazil's real currency, a newspaper said.

He said the balance of payments current account deficit, which amounted to $29.8 billion, or 3.9 percent, of gross domestic product (GDP) in the last 12 months, was "easily financed", according to O Globo.
The deficit could be financed through long-term investments and direct foreign investment which should amount to more than $15 billion this year, Loyola said.
He said the government would use monetary policy to combat the deficit, especially those measures which contain consumer demand, O Globo said.
He said the current account deficit was the result of heavy investments prompted by the restructuring of Brazil's manufacturing sector which made imports of primary resources and machinery necessary.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
